data.body: Fixes bug B-ci-gate-prints-passed-with-failing-tests. Write the regression test first and watch it FAIL on the unfixed code; then complete with --regression-test <test>.
data.title: Fix bug B-ci-gate-prints-passed-with-failing-tests: a passed command gate whose output lists failing tests

data.claim: run_command_gate classifies on exit code alone; flake accounting (_rerun_failed_tests/_account_flakes) runs only on FAILED results and never changes a verdict, so a command exiting 0 over output with FAILED lines is recorded passed with no rerun evidence. The doubled verdict is the nested command's 'ci: passed' in the tail plus run_text's 'ci: PASSED'.
data.falsifier: A gate whose command exits 0 and prints 'FAILED tests/x.py::t' ends non-passed or carries rerun evidence on the unfixed code
data.mechanism: classify_exit -> PASSED when code==0; failed_tests evidence is lifted regardless; no code path reruns on a pass
data.probe: pytest tests/test_gate_passed_with_failures.py on unfixed code
data.probe_output: unit_tests: PASSED after output 'FAILED tests/test_x.py::test_a - boom' / 'unit_tests: passed' (4 failed on old code, assert code==1 got 0). The original dx-round-justified command could not be inspected; its own retry is unverified, but ddflow could not tell either way: no rerun evidence existed.
data.question: Is the ci 'passed' with 5 listed failing tests a legitimate recorded rerun or a false pass?

evidence.note: R-ci-pass-with-failures CONFIRMED: probe reproduced PASSED over a FAILED line on old code
ddflow brief --item read; no rule contradicts: change is gate-verdict hardening
commit 0e9522a8c; tests/test_gate_passed_with_failures.py 4 pass, failed on old code

chunk_findings.detail: An event that records failures only via `failed_tests_more`, with `failed_tests == []`, still yields a pass. Given `result="passed"` and `ev = {"failed_tests": [], "failed_tests_more": 3}`, `not ids` is true, so the function returns `("passed", "")` without inspecting `failed_tests_more`. The gate then still reports passed despite the event indicating failing tests, which is the exact bug this change is meant to fix. The guard must also treat a positive `failed_tests_more` as a non-pass condition.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/api/gate_passed_failures.py:35

chunk_findings.detail: When `PF.apply` returns a failed rerun, `gate_baseline` returns immediately and skips the baseline-red downgrade required by its own contract. For a test listed in the passed command’s output that fails on the rerun and also fails on the base commit, the function returns `("failed", ...)`, but the contract says every failing test failing on the base too should produce `("partial", ...)`. The comment “the base has nothing to add” is false for this path.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/api/gate_baseline.py:24

chunk_findings.detail: For a failed rerun with no `failed_tests` in its revision, the `flaked` list is wrongly set to all original ids. Example: original ids `["a", "b"]`, rerun returns `("failed", {"failed_tests": []})` (e.g., pytest crashes before collecting a still-failing test). Then `[t for t in ids if t not in still]` becomes `["a", "b"]`, falsely marking both as flaked even though neither had a recorded passing rerun. Tests should only be marked flaked when they actually passed on rerun.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/api/gate_passed_failures.py:57

chunk_findings.detail: If `out.data["evidence"]["tail"]` is JSON `null`, then `ev.get("tail", "")` returns `None`, and `run_text` now passes that `None` straight into `_without_own_verdict`, where `tail.rstrip().splitlines()` raises `AttributeError: 'NoneType' object has no attribute 'rstrip'`. The previous code assigned `tail = ev.get("tail", "")` and then checked `if tail`, so `None` was treated as “no tail” and `run_text` returned `head` normally. This is a regression for nullable `evidence.tail` values.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/surfaces/declared/lifecycle_cli.py:_without_own_verdict

chunk_findings.detail: `test_the_log_prints_one_verdict` never actually requires one verdict line. The assertion is `len(verdicts) <= 1`, so an empty `verdicts` list passes, and the following `not any(...)` check is vacuously true when there are no matching lines. A regression where `_without_own_verdict` removes the command's own `unit_tests: passed` and fails to emit the replacement gate verdict would still leave this test green, even though the docstring and test name say the log must print ONE verdict line.
chunk_findings.title: tests/test_gate_passed_with_failures.py:92-93

chunk_findings.detail: `gate_baseline.apply` now returns immediately whenever `gate_passed_failures.apply` returns a non-empty reason. That skips the existing baseline-red path in the exact case where every failing test also fails on the base. For example, with `result="passed"` and `ev={"failed_tests": ["test_x"]}`, if the rerun returns `("failed", {"failed_tests": ["test_x"]})` and `test_x` also fails on the baseline, this function returns `("failed", "...")`. The function’s own contract says it should return `("partial", "<baseline-red reason>")` when every failing test fails on the base, so this can falsely fail a change for a pre-existing breakage.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/api/gate_baseline.py:16

chunk_findings.detail: `_without_own_verdict` drops the last tail line whenever it textually equals `<gate>: passed`, but it has no way to know that line came from the nested `ddflow ci` rather than from the gate command itself. For a gate named `deploy` whose command prints `deploy: passed` and then exits nonzero, with `out.data["outcome"] == "failed"` and `out.data["evidence"]["tail"] == "deploy: passed\n"`, the helper returns `""`, so `run_text` returns only `deploy: FAILED` and suppresses the command’s own evidence line. This is wrong for arbitrary user-configured command gates.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/surfaces/declared/lifecycle_cli.py:_without_own_verdict

chunk_findings.detail: When the rerun itself exhibits the same exit-0-with-failing-tests behavior this change is meant to catch, `rerun` can return `("passed", {"failed_tests": ["test_x"]})` (e.g. `gdef.command` is a masking wrapper and `TS.run_command` preserves its exit-0 behavior). Then `still = ["test_x"]` and `ok` is false, so the code falls through to the reason string and chooses `'did not run'` because `outcome != "failed"`; it returns `("unavailable", "exit 0, but the output lists 1 test failing and the rerun alone did not run (test_x). NOT a pass.")`. That reason is factually wrong, and because `gate_baseline.apply` returns immediately for any non-`"failed"` outcome, it skips `BR.on_base`, so it cannot return the baseline-red `"partial"` even when `test_x` also fails on the base.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/api/gate_passed_failures.py:64-67

chunk_findings.detail: The new `outcome == "passed"` guard fixes the prior failed-run example, but the helper still cannot distinguish a nested `ddflow ci` verdict line from the gate command’s own output when the gate passes. If a gate named `deploy` runs a plain command that prints `deploy: passed` and exits 0, with `out.data["outcome"] == "passed"` and `ev["tail"] == "deploy: passed\n"`, then `_without_own_verdict` returns `""` and `run_text` returns only `deploy: PASSED`, dropping the command’s actual stdout evidence. The previous probe only covers a failed run, so this passed-run case still demonstrates the same line-origin ambiguity.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/surfaces/declared/lifecycle_cli.py:_without_own_verdict

chunk_findings.detail: `apply` correctly treats an initial gate result as not a pass when it exits 0 over `failed_tests_more > 0`, but when judging the rerun it only checks `rev.get("failed_tests")`, ignoring `rev.get("failed_tests_more")`. A rerun can still exhibit the same mask: for example, the initial result is `("passed", {})` with `ev["failed_tests"] == ["test_a"]` and `ev["failed_tests_more"] == 0`; the selected-test rerun exits 0 and its output contains one failing test that is reported only as `failed_tests_more = 1` with `failed_tests == []` (a wrapper prints “1 test failed” but no node id). Then `ok` is true and `apply` returns `("passed", "passed after rerunning 1 test: test_a, each passed on rerun")`, allowing the gate to pass over a failing rerun output—the exact bug this module exists to prevent.

chunk_findings.detail: `_without_own_verdict` runs `tail.rstrip().splitlines()` over the entire evidence `tail` before `run_text` ever applies the existing `tail[-1200:]` display bound. A passed gate whose command emitted a very large tail (for example a test-suite run with hundreds of MB of captured output) now allocates a list of every line just to inspect the last one, materially increasing peak memory and possibly causing an OOM; the old path only sliced the final 1200 characters. Inspect only the last line, e.g. with `tail.rsplit("\n", 1)` or `tail.rpartition("\n")`, before truncating.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/surfaces/declared/lifecycle_cli.py:_without_own_verdict

chunk_findings.detail: This regression test does not exercise the confirmed `failed_tests_more` hole it was added to cover. With `broken="mask"`, the fake single-test pytest output is `FAILED tests/test_x.py::test_a - boom` followed by `1 failed in 0.1s`, so the rerun evidence still contains `failed_tests` with `tests/test_x.py::test_a`. The prior buggy `apply` that only checks `rev.get("failed_tests")` would see that non-empty list and reject the rerun, so this test passes on the unfixed code. To observe the `failed_tests_more` guard, the mask branch would need to emit only a summary failure (`1 failed in 0.1s` or `1 test failed`) with no `FAILED <node-id>` line. As written, the confirmed bug can return while this test stays green.

chunk_findings.detail: `not_a_failure` only treats pytest exits 4 and 5 as non-failures. A pre-fix run interrupted by the user/timeout (pytest exit code 2) or one that hits pytest internal error (exit code 3) can produce no parseable summary counts. For example, with `pre_ev = {"exit": 2, "summary": []}`, `ev.get("exit") in NO_TEST_RAN` is False and `_counts` returns `{}`, so the function returns `""`. `mutation.py` then treats the pre-fix run as a real pre-fix failure because `if unproven:` is false. That can close/accept a guard whose test was interrupted or errored internally, never actually demonstrating a failure before the fix.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/services/gates/regression_run.py:not_a_failure

data.probe: not_a_failure({'exit': 2, 'summary': []}) returned '' before; now a reason (test_a_run_that_ended_without_a_test_failure_did_not_fail_before)
data.title: ddflow/services/gates/regression_run.py:not_a_failure

chunk_findings.detail: The added `if isinstance(code, int) and code != 1:` early return bypasses the parsed pytest summary. pytest exits 2 when execution is interrupted, but if a test failed before the interrupt the summary may still report `1 failed`. For `ev = {"exit": 2, "summary": ["1 failed, 1 passed in 1.00s"]}`, `not_a_failure` returns a non-empty “ended without a test failure” reason, even though the run contains an actual test failure and the function’s own contract says it should return `""` when the test did fail. `mutation.py` would then treat a real pre-fix failure as merely unproven. The code should parse `_counts(ev)` for exit 2/3 and let a `failed` count win.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/services/gates/regression_run.py:not_a_failure

chunk_findings.detail: A strict-xfail test that unexpectedly passes is still counted as a real pre-fix failure. pytest reports `@pytest.mark.xfail(strict=True)` XPASS as `1 failed, 1 xpassed in 1.00s` and exits 1. For `ev = {"exit": 1, "summary": ["1 failed, 1 xpassed in 1.00s"]}`, `_counts` returns `{"failed": 1, "xpassed": 1}`, so `not_a_failure` reaches `counts and not counts.get("failed")`, sees `failed` is truthy, and returns `""`. The verifier then treats the run as “failed on the pre-fix tree” even though the test’s assertion actually passed; the same module already treats `xpassed` as not-a-pass in `not_a_pass`, so this is a false acceptance of an invalid guard.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/services/gates/regression_run.py:not_a_failure

data.title: ddflow/services/gates/regression_run.py:not_a_failure

chunk_findings.detail: The predicate `counts and (not counts.get("failed") or counts.get("xpassed"))` is too broad: any `xpassed` suppresses an actual `failed` count. For a run with one ordinary failing test plus one non-strict xfail that unexpectedly passes, pytest exits 1 and prints `"1 failed, 1 xpassed in 1.00s"`, so `_counts` returns `{"failed": 1, "xpassed": 1}`. `not_a_failure` then returns “the named test did not FAIL…” because `counts.get("xpassed")` is truthy, even though a real test failed on the pre-fix tree. The verifier would treat that run as a gap rather than a valid pre-fix failure, refusing a valid guard. The xpassed override needs to reflect strict-xfail attribution, not merely the presence of any xpassed.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/services/gates/regression_run.py:65 not_a_failure

chunk_findings.detail:
The new assertion requires `not_a_failure` to return a truthy reason for
`{"exit": 1, "summary": ["1 failed, 1 xpassed in 1s"]}`. That summary is ambiguous:
pytest emits the same line both for one strict-xfail XPASS (not a real test failure)
and for a run with one ordinary failed test plus one non-strict `@pytest.mark.xfail`
xpass (two collected tests, exit 1). In the second case there is a real pre-fix
failure, so the verifier should treat it as failed before, not as `could-not-run`.
The prior strict-xpass probe only proves the first case; it does not prevent this
over-corrected behavior from hiding a mixed run with a genuine failure.

chunk_findings.detail: The new early exit `return REGRESSION_COULD_NOT_RUN` fires whenever `not_a_pass(fix_ev, strict=True)` sees any fixed-tree failure. That is the wrong status for a real failure. For example, `--regression-test test_x` where `test_x` runs and fails on the fixed tree after passing on the pre-fix tree: the verifier should report `REGRESSION_FAILS_ON_FIX` (a blocking gate result), but this branch returns `REGRESSION_COULD_NOT_RUN` before the pre-fix tree is checked, misclassifying a definitive fixed-tree test failure as “could not run” and hiding the failing gate.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/services/gates/mutation.py:350-352

chunk_findings.detail: `_NOT_RUN` includes `"xpassed"`, and `not_a_pass` counts it as a skipped/xfail non-pass. But pytest reports `xpassed` when an xfail-marked test actually passed; that is a passing run. Given `ev = {"exit": 0, "summary": ["1 xpassed in 0.12s"]}`, `not_a_pass(ev, where="pre-fix tree", strict=False)` returns the non-pass gap instead of `""`. A pre-fix xpass means the test already passes before the fix, so `verify_regression_test` should still report that it PASSES on the pre-fix tree and reject the guard, not say there is no evidence either way.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/services/gates/regression_run.py:_NOT_RUN

chunk_findings.detail: The assertion `assert not_a_failure({"exit": 1, "summary": ["1 failed, 1 xpassed in 1s"]}, where="x")` is missing the `== ""` check. The preceding assertions show `not_a_failure` returns a string and returns `""` when the run did have a test failure. Since the summary contains `"1 failed"`, a correct `not_a_failure` must return `""`, so this bare assert evaluates `assert ""`, which is false and makes the test itself fail on the intended correct implementation. It should be `assert not_a_failure(...) == ""`.
chunk_findings.title: tests/test_regression_skip_not_pass.py:101
